blocks.md: **AB 1228, enacted in September 2023, raised the wage floor for large fast-food chains to \$20 an hour on April 1, 2024, when the general state minimum was \$16: a 25% increase, to about 77% of the state's median hourly wage. Limited-service restaurant earnings rose about 7 log points relative to states at the \$7.25 federal minimum. The employment estimate depends heavily on how the counterfactual is built.**

| Method | Earnings | Employment | Own-wage elasticity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Conventional DiD | +7.50 (0.81) | −1.39 (0.44) | −0.19 (0.06) |
| Synthetic DiD | +6.99 (0.71) | −0.26 (0.54) | −0.04 (0.08) |

Log points (≈ percent), average of 2024Q2–2025Q3 relative to 2023Q4; standard errors in parentheses. Conventional triple-difference estimates range from −0.38 to −2.19 depending on the comparison industry; synthetic triple differences are all close to zero.

| Method | Earnings | Employment | Separation rate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Conventional DiD | +7.62 | −0.34 | −12.74 |
| Synthetic DiD | +5.60 | +0.74 | −18.97 |

Average of 2024Q2–2024Q4 relative to 2023Q4. Across 16 QWI specifications employment ranges from about −0.6% to +1.7% (12 of 16 non-negative). Dube's reading: higher pay reduced quits, helping firms retain workers.

sections.heading: Clemens, Edwards, Meer and Nguyen (2026): 1,440 synthetic Californias

blocks.md: Crossing data source (QCEW, QWI), donor pool (20 federal-minimum states or all 48), outcome (5 definitions), seasonal adjustment (3), trend adjustment (3) and matching window (5) gives 900 SDID and 540 synthetic-control specifications through 2025Q4.

| Panel | Median employment effect |
| --- | --- |
| QCEW, SDID | −3.58% |
| QWI, SDID | −2.90% |
| QCEW, SC | −3.12% |
| QWI, SC | −2.43% |

96.3% of the estimates are negative (53 of 1,440 positive). Detrending matters most: relative to no detrending, annual detrending shifts the median by −2.15 to −2.98 percentage points; but even without detrending the median two-year SDID estimate is −2.83%.
